recipes.name: The Best Chicken Fried Steak
ingredients_raw: kosher salt and ground black pepper to taste

steps.text: Place steaks between two sheets of heavy plastic on a solid, level surface; firmly pound with a meat mallet to a ¼-inch thickness.
Place 2 cups flour in a shallow bowl.
Combine baking powder, baking soda, 1 teaspoon pepper, and ¾ teaspoon salt in a separate shallow bowl; stir in buttermilk, egg, Tabasco, and garlic to combine.
Heat shortening in a deep cast-iron skillet to 325 degrees F (165 degrees C). Place a wire rack over a sheet of parchment paper.

Meanwhile, dredge 1 steak in flour to coat; shake off excess. Dip into buttermilk batter; lift up so excess batter drips back into the bowl. Dredge in flour again to coat both sides completely. Place breaded steak on the prepared wire rack. Repeat with remaining steaks.
Fry steaks, in batches if necessary, until evenly golden brown, 3 to 5 minutes per side. Transfer steaks to a paper towel-lined plate to drain. Cover with foil to keep warm.
Drain fat from the skillet, reserving ¼ cup and as much solid remnants as possible.
Place skillet over medium-low heat. Add reserved ¼ cup oil; whisk in remaining ¼ cup flour. Scrape the brown bits of food off the bottom of the skillet with a spatula.
Stir in milk; increase heat to medium and bring gravy to a simmer. Cook, stirring often, until thick, 6 to 7 minutes. Season gravy with salt and black pepper.
Transfer steaks to a platter; pour gravy over top.

raw_recipe.headline: The Best Chicken Fried Steak
raw_recipe.description: This chicken fried steak recipe is a Southern favorite. It features crispy, breaded cube steaks drenched in a creamy gravy. It'll be a hit with everyone.

video.description: There’s no better comfort food than southern comfort food. In this video, Nicole shows you how to make chicken fried steak. First, after flattening out the steaks, whisk together some baking powder, baking soda, pepper, and salt. Now, combine the mixture with buttermilk, egg, hot sauce, and garlic to make the batter. Drudge and cover both sides of the steaks with flour and batter before frying in the pan of vegetable shortening oil. After the steaks finish frying, make sure to save some fat and solid remnants to whip up some gravy. Pour the gravy and enjoy this southern recipe!

review.reviewBody: This recipe is awesome! My family loved it. To fix the buttermilk dilemma some reviews have mentioned, try this: to make substitute buttermilk, add 1-3/4 tablespoons of cream of tartar to a cup of milk, or add a tablespoon of lemon juice or white vinegar to a cup of milk and let it stand for 5 to 10 minutes. In many baking recipes, you can also just use plain yogurt or sour cream instead of buttermilk. I use the vinegar method but the rest are good to know. I never buy buttermilk anymore because I never use the whole carton. Buttermilk is one of those where I could have it for weeks then not need it, as soon as it goes bad I need it. This is handy to keep in your box for any recipe calling for buttermilk, when in a pinch use a substitute.
Yum! I recommend salt and peppering the meat before dipping it in the flour and buttermilk mixture. Otherwise, the meat itself tastes bland.

Very good!! This recipe is basically how my family has made CFS for generations. For the gravy, I started with 2 cups chicken broth/bouillion and 2 cups milk. We used to use the left over water from when we boiled the potatoes for mashed potatoes. Then added the milk for cream gravy. For lumpless gravy.... add the salt to the flour and make sure the flour is cooked BEFORE you add the liquid ingredients.

Delicious. I didn't add as much Tabasco as called for because I only had a bottle of hot sauce (not Tabasco) and was afraid it would be too hot. I also prefer a beef gravy, so I used my homemade beef stock and some milk to make mine :) Yummy!

Initially made as written. Like many others, found it to be a bit bland (personal taste & will not reduce the rating for that!). After checking out many reviews, used paper towels to soak up as much moisture as possible, then seasoned the meat with seasonings that our family likes, allowing it to sit for 10 minutes, then soaked up more moisture. We season the buttermilk mixture AND the flour dredge (trust me, it’s not too much seasoning). After the final dredge in flour, placed on a wire rack and stuck it in the fridge for at least 30 minutes. Check the temperature of the oil prior to cooking, and followed cooking directions from there (except we placed the steaks on a wire rack, not paper towels. It can be placed in a 200 degree oven to keep warm while making the gravy). Did not have any of the coating come off. Still experimenting with the gravy. Going to try 1/2 buttermilk & 1/2 milk (we agree with others that 4 cups of milk is too much, 2 cups works better).

This was a wonderful recipe for chicken fried steak. Flavors were amazing. I did not have shortening or buttermilk on hand, so I substituted canola oil and 2% milk. They worked out just fine. The steak is best cooked in the cast iron skillet as recommended in the recipe as it cooks evenly and you have no problems with the steak sticking to the pan as long as you do not cook on too high a heat. Thanks so much for this great recipe. Family loved it and I will be making it again!

I made this according to the recipe mostly but my gravy was too thick... I did add to my meat brazillian steak seasoning thyme as well as the salt n pepper and I did same to my flour mixture... After battering the meat I set in fridge for 30 min and my batter never fell off my meat during the cooking process... When making the gravy I used flour from the meat that was reserved and I used light cream instead of buttermilk... The flavors were there the food was delicious

I followed the recipe exactly and it was delicious! It was pretty easy to follow and come out great! Definitely recommend! I did take some reviewer’s advice and put the battered steaks in the fridge for about an hour before frying. The costing did stay on. The only change I made was I fried them in avocado oil just because of my husband’s health. I don’t think it took away from the taste at all though. I’ll be making this again!

This was very good.make sure to season the meat before the breading process.Made this again and pretty much doubled the spices minus the the hot sauce. Used less than a cup of canola oil (vs shortening) The baking powder and soda make this the best I've ever made!Next I'm using this on chicken!

I have attempted to make chicken fried steak many times before, all attempts were unsuccessful, until this recipe! It was easy & delicious! The only change I made was to use 2 cups of milk and two cups of beef stock for the gravy. Yum, can't wait to make it again.

This was delicious. I did as others suggested...salt and peppered the steak prior to adding the coatings. I also used the rack to hold the meat so it wouldn't get soggy. Will definitely make this again.

It was bland even when seasoning the meat first. Really felt the spices should have been added to the flour rather than the buttermilk mixture. Also, all the oil should have been poured off and butter melted in the pan to make the gravy for more flavor. I made a half recipe for two people and the half recipe of egg/buttermilk mixture and flour mixture was was too much....a waste.
Made it exactly as written. It was amazing!!
Even a 70 year old man can make this wonderful recipe, my mom used to say when you have lumpy gravy, you drowned the miller. . It’s all good. Tks

Delicious! Be sure to add the hot sauce. I used Louisiana, but my wife couldn't even tell there was hot sauce in it, but I'm sure it adds to the total flavor. Followed the recipe exactly, and it was amazing. I didn't use a cast iron skillet, but as long as the temperature is right, it cooks up perfectly. I also didn't follow the gravy recipe, because I have my own recipe, but the steak was phenomenal.

My husband LOVED the chicken fried steaks I made following this recipe! I didn't have buttermilk so I used whole milk. We're southerners in Charleston SC....Hubby has eaten chicken fried steak since he was a youngster and he said this was the BEST he's ever had! 🙂 Great recipe!!!!
Terrible.
I added more salt to everything and instead of Tabasco, I use Sriracha. It was delicious.
A 10 out of 10 especially when paired with white gravy from scratch and mint cucumber salad.
Good flavor, good "crunch". Next time I may cut my cube steaks in more manageable pieces. Breading process definitely messy!
